title: Constrained Central Cavity with Narrowed Spacer Bounds (250-420 nm)
scientific_hypothesis: Constraining the central spacer layers (layers 3-7) to a narrower 250-420 nm thickness range will increase the cavity quality factor and sharpen the emissivity peak in the 8000-13000 nm band while maintaining out-of-band suppression in 3000-5000 nm.
design_principle: Defect cavity microresonator with periodic Bragg reflectors on both sides of a central defect region. Narrower thickness bounds on spacer layers reduce design space variance, promoting higher Q-factor resonance without breaking alignment.
proposed_topology: 17-layer fixed sequence: Air | [HfO2/SiO2]_8 reflector | SiO2 defect spacer | [SiO2/HfO2]_8 reflector | Si substrate. Exact layer count: 17 finite layers.
design_variables: layer thicknesses with layer-specific bounds: layers 1-2 and 8-17 at 200-3000 nm, layers 3-7 constrained to 250-420 nm
manufacturing_considerations: thickness bounds reflect plasma-enhanced ALD capability for HfO2/SiO2
narrower central bounds may improve fabrication tolerance
theory_basis: Transfer Matrix Method for multilayer interference
Kirchhoff's law relating emissivity to absorptance
Defect cavity resonance theory for spectral selectivity
expected_advantages: Higher Q-factor from constrained spacer variance
Sharper emissivity peak in target band
Improved robustness from reduced thickness sensitivity in central region
known_risks: Over-constraint may limit optimizer ability to find global optimum
Narrow bounds may prevent resonance alignment if initial guess is poor
execution_request_english: Optimize a 17-layer HfO2/SiO2 defect cavity on Si substrate with air incidence. Layer sequence: HfO2, SiO2, HfO2, SiO2, HfO2, SiO2, HfO2, SiO2, SiO2 (defect), HfO2, SiO2, HfO2, SiO2, HfO2, SiO2, HfO2, SiO2. Thickness bounds: layers 1-2 and 8-17 bounded 200-3000 nm; layers 3-7 bounded 250-420 nm. Optimize all layer thicknesses using gradient-based optimizer to maximize mean absorptance in 8000-13000 nm wavelength band and minimize mean absorptance in 3000-5000 nm band. Assume normal incidence, unpolarized light. Use HfO2 and SiO2 refractive index data from material registry for mid-IR range. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 3000-5000 nm, 8000-13000 nm. soft objectives: high emissivity in 8000-13000 nm; low emissivity in 3000-5000 nm. behaviors to suppress or avoid: high emissivity in 3000-5000 nm. manufacturing constraints: total layer count not exceeding 24.
revision_reason: Applied feedback directive to constrain central spacer layers 3-7 to 250-420 nm range to increase cavity Q-factor while preserving outer reflector optimization freedom. Differs from prior iterations by implementing narrower bounds on specific layers rather than uniform bounds.
